findings.description: The bucket is explicitly documented as public with no ACL restricting access, allowing unauthenticated or unauthorized read/write access to stored data, including a sensitive customer master file.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including sensitive customer data) are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, meaning objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, increasing the risk of undetected data tampering or loss, especially combined with public access.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in public, unencrypted bucket
findings.description: A customer master spreadsheet (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and lacks server-side encryption, directly exposing sensitive customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, allowing financial data objects to be overwritten or deleted without the ability to recover prior versions.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so operational data stored in this bucket is not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, leaving data science datasets unencrypted at rest despite having logging and versioning enabled.
